events.name: 502 errors begin on API
events.description: API begins returning 502 Bad Gateway at 10:00 (T+0). This is the first observable symptom.

events.name: CPU alert fires on worker-3
events.description: CPU threshold breach alert triggers on worker-3 at 10:04 (T+4), four minutes after the first 502.

events.name: Upstream deploy completes
events.description: Upstream service deployment finishes at 10:07 (T+7), seven minutes after errors started and three minutes after CPU alert.

events.name: Upstream deploy in progress (inferred)
events.description: The deploy was necessarily in flight before T+0, since it completed at T+7. Start time unknown but constrained to before 10:00. This is the causally relevant state — not the completion event.

relations.note: Mechanism: rolling deploy creates a mixed-version upstream; new code version introduces incompatibility or the restart cycle makes some backends temporarily unavailable, triggering 502s. The 0-minute delay at onset is consistent with a hard-break compatibility issue vs. a gradual degradation.

Mechanism: 502 errors generate aggressive client retries; retry storm accumulates over ~4 minutes until CPU threshold is breached on worker-3. Alternatively, error-handling code paths (logging, circuit breakers) are more compute-intensive than the happy path.

TEMPORAL PARADOX — REFUTED. The deploy completion at T+7 cannot cause errors at T+0. The effect precedes the purported cause by 7 minutes. The naive hypothesis 'deploy caused errors' is only valid if reframed as the in-progress deploy state (r1), not the completion event.

constraints.subject: deploy_complete
constraints.note: This constraint directly falsifies any causal model where the deploy *completion* is the trigger. It does NOT falsify the deploy *process* as a cause.
